findings.source_quote: καὶ ὅσοι, φησίν, ἐξ αὐτῶν μετανενοήκασι, τὴν κατοικίαν εἰς τὸν πύργον ἔχουσιν· ὅσοι δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν βραδύτερον μετανενοήκασιν, εἰς τὰ τείχη κατοικήσουσιν
findings.english_quote: The working text has “have repented,” including the slower group; Michigan uses future repentance verbs here, Bonner printed pp. 105–106, with some damaged letters. Alternative: “Those among them who have repented have their dwelling in the tower. Those who repent more slowly will dwell in the walls. Those who do not repent but persist in their deeds will surely die.”
findings.issue: Footnote b reports plural future repentance verbs in Michigan, but its alternative retains “have repented” for the first group and changes only the slower group's repentance wording. Consequently, the note does not clearly identify or represent the reported tense differences. The supplied comparison report does not transcribe the relevant vii.3 forms, so it cannot resolve this discrepancy.
findings.suggested_revision: Supply the located project transcription or comparison report identifying each differing repentance verb and its preserved or restored letters. Then make the alternative consistently represent that report, or narrow the claim if only the slower group's verb differs. Retain the selected working reading in the main text. Any replacement note requires fresh review.

Revise the alternative or narrow the report accordingly, without changing the source-compatible main text merely because a variant exists. Review the replacement afresh.

summary: Both main texts were independently checked against every supplied Greek clause. They preserve the rod groups, repentance distinctions, negations, speaker reporting, tower/walls outcomes, and life-and-death assertions; bracketed editorial supplements are explicitly distinguished from preserved reporting expressions. Both require a limited correction or supporting evidence for footnote b's inconsistent presentation of the reported Michigan tense alternatives. This is a review of the supplied source and disclosures, not authentication of unseen manuscripts or exhaustive collation.
